cards.text: One Sabbath, Jesus is teaching in one of the synagogues. Everybody's settled in, listening, same seats as always. Friend, mark it down: this is NOT about to be a same-seats-as-always kind of day.
There's a woman in that synagogue who's been disabled by a spirit. She's hunched over and can't stand up straight.

cards.question: How long has the hunched-over woman in the synagogue been disabled?

cards.text: Eighteen YEARS, friend, and I start pacing when my oven takes ten minutes to preheat. Right in the middle of His teaching, Jesus sees her.

cards.question: When Jesus sees the hunched-over woman during His teaching, what does He do?

answers.text: He calls her over to Him
He finishes teaching and finds her later
He sends His disciples to bring her outside

cards.question: Jesus tells the woman she is set free from her disability.

cards.text: Then Jesus places His hands on her. Eighteen years of staring at the floor, and the Lord's hands are on her shoulders.

cards.question: After Jesus places His hands on the woman, how soon does she straighten up?
Standing straight for the first time in eighteen years, the woman begins to ___.

cards.text: She's standing tall and glorifying God, right there in the synagogue. And the synagogue leader is INDIGNANT, like somebody just stamped a batch of cookies right on his good tablecloth.

cards.question: Why is the synagogue leader indignant after the woman is healed?

answers.text: Jesus touched a woman in public

cards.question: The indignant synagogue leader takes his complaint straight to Jesus.

cards.text: He tells the crowd, "There are six days for work," and then, "So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath." A woman stands up straight for the first time in eighteen years, and this man pulls out the CALENDAR.
Upset about Jesus, talking to EVERYBODY. That's the guy who's mad at one coworker and hits reply-all on the whole company. And the Lord answers, "You hypocrites!"

cards.question: Jesus asks about something each of them does for his ox or donkey on the Sabbath. What is it?

answers.text: Unties it from the stall and leads it to water
Leaves it tied in the stall until evening
Brushes it down and lets it rest all day

cards.question: Jesus has just pointed out that they untie their animals on the Sabbath. So what does He say about this woman?

answers.text: She should be released on the Sabbath too
She could have waited one more day
She should have asked the leader first

cards.text: And listen to what Jesus calls her: a daughter of Abraham. Not "the Sabbath problem," friend. FAMILY.

cards.question: Jesus says it is Satan who has kept this woman bound for eighteen long years.
When Jesus says this, all His adversaries are ___, and the whole crowd ___ at all the glorious things He's doing.

findings.problem: The tablecloth comparison doesn't match the core action. The leader is indignant that Jesus healed on the Sabbath, which means doing something on the wrong day. Stamping cookies on someone's tablecloth is about making a mess or damaging his things, so the comparison has a different action and won't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Upset about Jesus, talking to EVERYBODY.", the reply-all line, and "And the Lord answers, 'You hypocrites!'" It isn't the opening card, so it is limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "And listen to what Jesus calls her: a daughter of Abraham.", "Not 'the Sabbath problem,' friend." and "FAMILY." It isn't the opening card, so it is limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question opens with "When Jesus says this." The word "this" points back to His words about the animals and the daughter of Abraham, which were on earlier cards that are no longer on screen. The question needs to say what Jesus said.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. Of the 11 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice (cards 3, 5, 8, 11, 15, 16), 3 are true or false and 2 are fill in the blank. That is three times as many multiple choice cards as fill in the blank cards.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
